**▶▶▶ CYCLE 814 (2026-07-02) — R1 SURPASSED (6/6 seeds GO): the on-bridge HTM Temporal-Memory SCALES to n_seq=8 contexts sharing one middle. ROOT CAUSE (traced, not guessed): on the dense pre-allocated pool the host `_match_count` required a CONNECTED synapse (perm>=perm_conn=0.5) to count a "match", but a synapse only reaches 0.5 after ~4 potentiations → for the first epochs NO cell matched → the learner RE-ALLOCATED every epoch; with `_committed_count` saturating uniformly (all cells burst-winners → equal counts → the tiebreak collapses to INDEX ORDER), allocation became an index-order ROUND-ROBIN that ROTATED the context↔cell binding every epoch → at n_seq>=3 (>2 contexts/epoch) distinct contexts MERGED onto the same shared-middle cells → branch 0.000. The bridge WEIGHTED-coincidence PREDICTION was proven CLEAN (known-good connectivity → 1.000, zero over-firing) — 100% allocation. FIX: `_match_count` thresholds a match at the COMMITTED level (perm > p_init+0.02, the same threshold `_committed_count` uses) not CONNECTED — a once-potentiated cell (perm~0.14>0.02) matches IMMEDIATELY, so re-training REINFORCES the epoch-0 disjoint allocation instead of re-drawing it (== the numpy FlatHTM oracle's W>0 match). Untrained (perm=0) still matches 0 → still allocates (anti-cheats preserved). RESULT 6/6 seeds (42/43/44/100/101/102) n_seq=8/n_cells=40/epochs=80: **branch 1.000, dAP-lesion 0.000, untrained 0.000, oracle parity 1.000.** Finding: `2026-07-02-emerge14-onbridge-nseq-scaling-R1-surpassed-GO.md`. ⇒ the emergent sequence cortex now learns MANY-context high-order sequences on the real spiking substrate. R2 (multi-segment cell-reuse for MORE contexts than floor(n_cells/k_win) on a FIXED cell budget) stands as a characterized ranked-second lever (a small guarded `segment_id` mask dimension), NOT a wall.

## CRASH-RECOVERY (2026-05-28 ~17:32 EDT): D7 production died with Claude crash; relaunched with proper detachment

Claude desktop crashed during autoupdate (took D7 production PID 30216 with it -- I had wrongly claimed earlier it was "detached," but `-NoNewWindow` kept it attached to the harness's console process group, so the console tree got reaped). KILL-SAFE caches saved 12/15 cells (A_nouns, B_verbs, C_adj, D_spatial all 3 seeds; E_functional/seed42 was at 10%, lost the ~21 min partial).

Relaunched at 17:32:57 as PID 26928 with `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden` (creates a separate process group with its own console, no shared console with the harness -> survives client crashes). Cache-skip verified working (each of 12 cached cells "completes" in ~1.1 min by just loading the bridge + activity npz). Will then train E_functional seeds 42/43/44 (~225 min each), then run cross-bridge probe inline. ETA ~05-30 05:00 EDT.

LESSON for future launches: Use `-WindowStyle Hidden` (or omit `-NoNewWindow`) so the python process gets its own console + survives client death. `-NoNewWindow` is convenient for live log piping but makes the process die with the harness. The KILL-SAFE per-cell caches did their job here -- they're the load-bearing recovery mechanism, not the detachment.

## CYCLE 606 (2026-06-26 — recall-crash DIAGNOSED (offline, decisive): over-training DENSIFICATION, not read-out; fix = optimal window count at proven n_per / multi-bridge)

OWNER said "up to you" on the diagnosis fork -> ran the OFFLINE diagnostic (_diagnose_recall_degradation.py, CPU, no GPU): loaded the saved 150K brain's weights M + re-derived codes under 6 normalizations, re-measured recall. DECISIVE: NO norm recovers recall (saved log1p(M*100)=0.208, log1p(M)=0.125, log1p(M*10)=0.167, M-raw=0.125, sqrt=0.208, row-L2=0.208 -- all << the 8K's 0.917). => NOT a read-out/normalization issue; the LEARNED WEIGHTS degraded. MECHANISM = over-training DENSIFICATION: the 150K M is fully DENSE (frac-nonzero 1.0) with NO saturation (frac>0.9max = 0) -- over 150K windows every concept co-occurs with every frequent hub, so the DISTINGUISHING structure washes out into a uniform background -> codes blur -> recall collapses. 8K = sparse+structured = recall 0.917. WHY 320 survived (n_per 16-24, 150K, recall 1.0) but 1454 crashed: 1454 used n_per 10 (to fit single-bridge) on 4.5x the concepts -> more competition + smaller population + faster densification.

=> the BREADTH TARGET is sound (1454 fits, moat holds); a single over-trained 1454/n_per-10 bridge is the wrong vehicle. FIX: stay in the STRUCTURED regime -- train to the window count where recall PEAKS before densifying, at the proven n_per.
